questions.question: A sample of a gas occupies 500 cm³ at 27 °C and 1 atm pressure. Calculate the volume it will occupy at 127 °C if the pressure is kept constant. Assume the gas behaves ideally.
questions.solution:
At constant pressure, Charles's law applies: $\dfrac{V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{V_2}{T_2}$, with temperature in kelvin.

**Step 1 — Convert to kelvin**

$$T_1 = 27 + 273 = 300 \ \text{K}, \qquad T_2 = 127 + 273 = 400 \ \text{K}$$

**Step 2 — Apply the law**

$$\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2} \Rightarrow V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 500 \times \frac{400}{300}$$

$$V_2 = 666.7 \ \text{cm}^3$$

Since $T_2 > T_1$, the volume increases, as expected for Charles's law. If a balloon burst on a hot summer afternoon, this is exactly why.
questions.knowledgeNote: At constant pressure a gas volume is directly proportional to its absolute temperature in kelvin.
